environment.description: Same Rails application deployed inside a FreeBSD 14 jail (not Docker) with the process root set to /srv/app via chroot(2). The jail's securelevel is set to 3 and the process runs under a dedicated UID (nobody:nogroup equivalent). The jail's allow.raw_sockets is set to 0 and children.max=0. The host system applies a pf(4) rule with 'set timeout { adaptive.start 120, adaptive.end 600 }' on the jail's loopback interface and a ALTQ/CBQ scheduler with a fixed 50ms delay-bucket queue ('queue jitter_q bandwidth 100Kb cbq(default, rio)') applied to all egress traffic from the jail's vnet interface. The Puma workers inside the jail are pinned to a single cpuset with intentional noisy-neighbor cron jobs (find / -type f -exec sha256 {} \; running every 30s) to inject CPU scheduling variance. The combination of network-level jitter injection via ALTQ queuing discipline and CPU scheduling noise makes timing measurements statistically indistinguishable below the token comparison variance threshold.

config.network_shaping: pf ALTQ/CBQ queue 'jitter_q' bandwidth 100Kb with rio on jail vnet egress, adaptive timeouts start=120 end=600
config.noise_injection: cron job every 30s: find / -type f -exec sha256 {} \; within same cpuset
config.sensitive_files: No secret material in chroot beyond database-stored tokens (PostgreSQL socket outside jail, accessed via TCP to host)
